 Judgment

Dated this the 8th day of August, 2025 The 1st petitioner is a permanent employee of the Travancore Devaswom Board for the past 21 years and is presently working as a Sub-Group Officer at Ulloor Major Sree Subrahmanya Temple, under Ulloor Group.

2. The petitioners state that respondents 3 to 6, who are functionaries of the Temple Trust, continue to hold office illegally even after the expiry of their term in violation of the bye-laws of the Trust.

Serious allegations, including misappropriation of Temple ornaments and fabrication of records during General Body meetings, have led to the registration of Ext.P1 FIR against respondents 3 to 6 and others under Sections 406, 420, 465, 471 and 468 read with Section 34 of the IPC.
2025:KER:59454 3.
The 7th respondent is a close associate of respondents 3 to 6.
He is involved in several criminal cases and was detained under preventive detention.
The 7th respondent is used by respondents 3 to 6 to handle people who prefer complaints against them.
Ext.P2 is the FIR registered against the 7th respondent based on the complaint of the 2nd petitioner.
Respondents 3 to 7 are continuously threatening the petitioners and attempting to falsely implicate them in offences and to harm their personal and professional lives.
The petitioners and their families are living in constant fear for their lives and property.
The petitioners submitted complaints seeking police protection before respondents 1 and 2.
However, no action has been taken so far.

4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Government Pleader representing respondents 1 and 2.
2025:KER:59454 5.
The contention of the petitioners is that respondents 3 to 7 are consistently threatening the life of the petitioners and hence police protection is sought.
6. It is evident from the pleadings that on the basis of complaints filed by the petitioners, Ext.P2 FIR was lodged at the instance of the 2nd petitioner.

Ext.P2 FIR was registered on 01.05.2024.
7.

Though the petitioners have averred in the writ petition and the exhibits that respondents 3 to 7 are consistently threatening the petitioners to implicate them in false criminal cases, no specific instance has been brought to the notice of this Court in respect of the alleged threat.
8. In the circumstances, police protection cannot be granted.

However, if the petitioners face any actual physical threat or assault from the part of respondents 3 to 7, they will be free to bring it to the notice of the 2 nd respondent and in 2025:KER:59454 that case, the 2nd respondent shall look into the matter and take necessary action.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
